features.text: The patient has had trouble swallowing for the past four to five weeks.
The patient experiences a sensation of something being stuck in the throat, especially with solid foods like a sandwich.
The patient reports that the swallowing difficulty is not too bad most of the time but does bother him and sometimes feels a little painful.
The patient has not experienced weight loss.
The patient has not experienced chest or throat pain associated with dysphagia.
The patient has not been evaluated for this symptom before.
The patient has not experienced regurgitation, heartburn, or odynophagia.
The patient does not smoke or consume alcohol.
The patient has no history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).
The patient has not had any recent upper respiratory infections or throat irritation.
The patient does not have difficulty swallowing liquids.
The patient sometimes needs to wash down a bite of food to get it to go down.
The patient has not undergone any prior imaging or endoscopic evaluations of the throat or esophagus.
The patient has not experienced a sensation of food getting stuck in the chest or upper abdomen.
The patient has not had any changes in voice or difficulty breathing.
The patient is willing to undergo an upper endoscopy or barium swallow study to evaluate for possible structural or motility causes of dysphagia.
